reason: Unbuttressed = trunk base without buttresses: negation of FLOPO:0991138 buttressed, as unlobed = not lobed.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (place on the part: the veins, PO_0005020, of the bearer are red)
reason: The colour is in the veins, not in the whole petal or sepal: the bearer is the vein of the part and the quality is red. 'or -veined' is a fragment of a colour alternative.

The examples mix different things: glistening glands, crystal-like papillae on an anther cap, and crystals (druses, cystoliths) inside tissue. PATO crystal configuration is about molecular structure; no single plant quality is meant.
A seedless fruit or fruit segment has no seed: complement of has_part some seed, as ebracteate = bract absent.
Squat is a loose proportion (short for its width) with no measure or second term. It cannot be pinned to decreased height or increased thickness alone.

In floras, oval is used for the elliptic outline and PATO elliptic is defined as oval. 'Narrowly' only states the length-to-width ratio, which has no term of its own. Not PATO_0001891 ovate, whose 'oval' synonym is the egg shape.
A frequency cue ('flowers occasional', 'sporophytes occasional') that belongs in frequency_qualifier, not a quality of the part.
Diaphanous = thin enough to let light through: PATO translucent (low opacity). 'Slightly diaphanous' wings fit low opacity better than transparent.
A subshrub is woody only at the base: the existing FLOPO growth-form value suffrutescent habit, used on the whole plant (PO_0000003, which has suffrutex as a synonym).

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (compound of two values: acuminate PATO_0002228 and awn PO_0025349 present)
reason: A compound of two values that both hold: the apex tapers gradually (acuminate) and ends in an awn (aristate = awn present, rule C207). It needs no term of its own.
Pouch-like = shaped like a pouch or bag: FLOPO saccate, which already has pouched as a synonym.
Divided = split into parts (PATO split, the parent of laciniate and pedate). 'Irregularly' adds no separate quality, and laciniate would wrongly add narrow, pointed segments.

A leaning stem or trunk slants away from the vertical: PATO oblique orientation, which is also the parent of FLOPO descending. Leaning on neighbouring plants for support is already covered by the 'scrambling' rule (climbing).
Explicit negation of FLOPO sulcate (longitudinally grooved).

label: colony-forming
definition: An aggregated quality inhering in a whole plant by virtue of its spreading vegetatively, by rhizomes, stolons or root suckers, into a patch of connected or closely spaced shoots. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991007 caespitose (tufted from one base); not FLOPO:0991010 mat-forming, which is low and flat.
reason: Floras use 'forming extensive patches' for clonal spread, which neither caespitose (one tuft) nor mat-forming (low, flat) covers. PO lists clonal colony only as a synonym of whole plant.

label: napiform
definition: A convex 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like a turnip: broad and rounded above and abruptly narrowed below into a slender tip. NOTE: Distinct from FLOPO:0991077 turbinate (top-shaped, conical below) and PATO:0002400 fusiform.
reason: A standard botanical term for roots and tubers, with no PATO or FLOPO class.

target: docs/odp/03-count-of-parts.md (flower PO_0009046 in the inflorescence, increased amount PATO_0000470)
reason: Multiflorous = many-flowered, a count of flowers written as one word ('flowered' → flower in flora_counted_parts.tsv). With no number, the value is increased amount.
In moss floras, radiculose stems are covered with rhizoids ('radicles'): rhizoid present on the stem.
A spelling variant of the existing FLOPO bract-like.
Semiamplexicaul = clasping about half the stem. PATO clasping is defined as at least partly enclosing the axis, so it fits exactly. FLOPO amplexicaul is the full clasp.
Clathrate = latticed, a network of walls or veins with clear spaces between: FLOPO reticulate (forming a network). Not PATO cancellous, which is used for bone.
Semiglossy is a weaker degree of glossy, a 'sub-/semi-' approximate value of PATO glistening (synonym glossy). It needs no term of its own.
Venose = with evident veins, the same reading as the rule for 'veined' (C211).
Strumose = bearing a struma, a goitre-like swelling, usually on one side at the base of a moss capsule: FLOPO gibbous (swollen on one side). 'Not strumose' then negates gibbous.
Crestless = without a crest: negation of FLOPO crested.

label: synoicous
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in a bryophyte gametophyte by virtue of its bearing antheridia and archegonia mixed together in the same gametoecium. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991093 autoicous; bryophyte sexual system, distinct from flowering-plant monoecy.
reason: A standard term for a moss sexual condition, used beside the existing FLOPO autoicous and dioicous. No existing class covers male and female organs mixed in one gametoecium.

label: excurved
definition: A curved quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being curved outward, away from the axis or the centre of the structure that bears it. NOTE: PATO:0002211 recurved (backward or inward) and PATO:0001597 everted (turned outward in placement, not curved) do not fit.
reason: A common botanical curvature of apices, petals and style branches. The nearest PATO terms are either the wrong direction (recurved) or not a curvature (everted).
A shape between two values, like 'linear-lanceolate', which is already covered as a continuum. 'Broadly' only states the width.
Every stem has nodes, so 'noded' carries meaning only through its modifier (many-, densely, distantly): a count or spacing of stem nodes, not a quality term.
A compound of two outline values, handled like 'linear-lanceolate' as a continuum between them.
